misconceptions.description: Selecting a technology first and then searching for a problem it solves, instead of naming the value tension before the tool
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts a tool and only afterward asks what classroom problem it addresses
misconceptions.feedback: Reverse the order. Surface the competing classroom values first, then choose a tool to negotiate that named tension.

misconceptions.description: Mislabeling a logistical constraint such as teacher workload as the design tension, instead of the competing learning values
misconceptions.trigger: learner frames the tension around convenience rather than two values that both have a claim on the learning
misconceptions.feedback: Restate the tension as two learning values in conflict (for example, feedback speed vs. feedback depth), keeping workload as a constraint, not the tension itself.

misconceptions.description: Letting an AI tool recommendation stand in for the work of surfacing the value tension first
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts an AI 'best tool' suggestion without naming the competing values it must negotiate
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI to help enumerate the competing values, then evaluate any candidate tool against that named tension.

misconceptions.description: Believing a design tension is resolved by eliminating one value rather than negotiating a defensible position between both
misconceptions.trigger: learner declares a tension 'gone' after adopting a tool, hiding the value that was traded away
misconceptions.feedback: Show the negotiated position: what each value gained, what was given up, and why the trade is defensible here.
